command.description: Report the version of the selected Node executable.

pathCommand.description: Resolve the selected Node executable with the platform PATH resolver.

install.macos: Download the official macOS installer or binary from https://nodejs.org/en/download/.
install.windows: Download the official Windows installer from https://nodejs.org/en/download/.
install.repair: Install a supported LTS release, open a new shell, then rerun node --version and npm --version. Do not silently alter PATH.

command.description: Report the version of the selected Git executable.

pathCommand.description: Resolve the selected Git executable with the platform PATH resolver.

featureChecks.description: Confirm that the current directory is a Git repository.
Confirm that Git worktree listing is available.

install.macos: Run git --version to invoke Xcode Command Line Tools, or use the official installer at https://git-scm.com/install/mac.
install.windows: Install Git for Windows from https://git-scm.com/install/windows. The official page also documents winget.
install.repair: Start a new shell after installation, verify git --version, and use git config --list --show-origin when configuration precedence is suspect.

command.description: Report the version of the selected Codex executable.

authCommand.description: Check login state without printing credentials.

featureChecks.description: Confirm that non-interactive execution is available.
Read the feature set from the selected Codex executable.

detect.versionSource: The active codex executable reports its own version; do not duplicate it in this catalog.

install.macos: Use the official standalone installer https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh, npm install -g @openai/codex, or the documented Homebrew cask.
install.windows: Use the official PowerShell installer https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 or npm install -g @openai/codex. The native installer is distinct from WSL2 support.
install.login: After installation, run codex login and complete the user-controlled browser flow; verify with codex login status.
install.repair: Resolve the executable with the platform PATH command, remove ambiguity between standalone and npm-managed installs only with explicit user action, and rerun codex --version. Never print auth.json or tokens.

commands.description: Report the version of the ocx executable.
Report the version of the opencodex executable.

featureChecks.description: Confirm the local OpenCodex server and backend status.

detect.versionSource: plugins/oh-my-teams/package.json dependency version; this catalog must not define a second OpenCodex version constant.

install.macos: With Node and npm ready, install the exact dependency version declared by plugins/oh-my-teams/package.json using npm; no separate Bun installation is required by the official guide.
install.windows: With Node and npm ready, install the exact dependency version declared by plugins/oh-my-teams/package.json using npm. Windows execution is documented as an install path, not as a completed platform measurement.

accountCheck.description: Confirm exactly one account using machine-readable account metadata, then report only a secret-free label.

login.description: Log in exactly one user-selected account in a separate OPENCODEX_HOME. Do not read or copy existing Claude credentials. Block on missing, multiple, or secret-bearing account labels.

install.repair: Check both command names and PATH, compare the installed package version with package.json, and reinstall only in an owned staging prefix. Do not claim pool switching or automatic account changes from a healthy process alone.

command.description: Run the executable selected once by orca-adapter.mjs; do not choose a fallback after failure.

steps.description: Discover the version-matched Orca CLI guide.
Read status JSON and require app version, ready runtime identity, and capabilities.

featureChecks.description: Confirm worktree capability on the selected executable.
Confirm terminal capability on the selected executable.

install.macos: Install the official Orca desktop app from https://onorca.dev/download or use brew install --cask stablyai/orca/orca; verify the bundled CLI is on PATH.
install.windows: Install the official Windows .exe from https://onorca.dev/download or the Orca GitHub releases page; verify the CLI from the installed app is on PATH.
install.repair: Start a new shell, rerun orca --version, and rediscover the CLI/runtime pair when versions differ. Do not substitute another terminal or agent runtime.

binary.description: Reuse the executable selected by orca-adapter.mjs; a failed selection cannot trigger fallback.

detect.process: Orca desktop process must be observable on the host before GUI-dependent features are enabled.

featureChecks.description: Confirm that an owned worktree is visible in status JSON.
Confirm that the requested terminal capability is available.
Confirm that desktop runtime identity matches the selected CLI.

install.macos: Download the Apple Silicon or Intel desktop build from https://onorca.dev/download, or install the official Homebrew cask.
install.windows: Download and run the official Windows installer from https://onorca.dev/download.
install.repair: Launch Orca manually, confirm the app process and CLI report the same installation, then retry the requested capability. A CLI being present does not prove that the desktop service is running.

command.description: Report the version of the selected GitHub CLI executable.

authCommand.description: Check GitHub CLI login state without printing a token.

install.macos: Install from the official GitHub CLI page https://cli.github.com/ or use the documented Homebrew package.
install.windows: Install from the official GitHub CLI page https://cli.github.com/ using the documented Windows installer or winget path.
install.login: Run gh auth login and complete the user-controlled flow; verify with gh auth status. Do not expose gh auth token output.
install.repair: Check PATH, host selection, and repository access separately. Reauthenticate only when the user chooses it; a successful binary check is not an authentication check.
